A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete versions of the same survey, retaining the same central taxonomy, benchmark overview, two figures, and five tables. All pages support comparison; neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 presents literature synthesis, qualitative comparisons, and previously published dataset statistics. Its empirical performance figures are attributed to cited studies.

after.justification: v2 remains a survey. The expanded agent discussion presents literature-based recommendations and future directions, without original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The surveyed query rewriting, long-form answering, and clarification procedures are unchanged. Section 5.3 elaborates possible future agent designs without introducing a specified algorithm or model for this work.

E1.justification: Section 4 and Table 4 retain the same datasets and task categories. The new agentic and multilingual discussion does not establish additional training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. The surveyed methods in Tables 2–3 are unchanged; newly cited agent and judge methods are not experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The benchmark and metric descriptions in Section 4 remain unchanged. Section 5.3 recommends judge-based evaluation for future systems but introduces no evaluation protocol actually used by this work.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or empirical case studies. The expanded opportunities discussion supplies conceptual recommendations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Discussions of model uncertainty and clarification thresholds do not introduce statistical reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Dataset statistics and existing performance reports are unchanged, including 23.6% F1 in Section 2.3 and the cited 0.57 AUROC for LLaMA-2-13B-Chat and 0.53 F1 for GPT-3.5-Turbo in Section 5. No new concrete evaluation results are reported.

T1.justification: The ambiguity definitions and three-category taxonomy remain unchanged. Bayesian experimental design and expected information gain are newly discussed conceptually, without mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The title adds agents, and the abstract and conclusion explicitly emphasize agentic future directions. The central contributions concerning ambiguity taxonomy, three disambiguation policies, and benchmark synthesis remain intact.

C2.justification: The brief opportunities paragraph becomes a substantial Section 5.3 roadmap covering agent specifications, memory and verification, information-gain-based clarification, reward-driven coordination, judge-based policy assessment, and personalized clarification. This substantially expands the proposed mechanisms and practical implications. The existing Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 4 retains the same dataset access links. The revision adds no implementation settings, hardware information, reproducible training instructions, or code/data release information for this work.

R1.justification: Section 5.3 substantially extends the research context to multi-agent systems, active disambiguation, reinforcement learning, and LLM/agent judges. Additions include Kobalczyk et al. (2025), Mukherjee et al. (2025), and Zhuge et al. (2025); the earlier Wu et al. (2023) and Zeng et al. (2023) references are removed.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains numbered subsections 5.1–5.3, and Opportunities is rewritten into several thematic discussions. The title, abstract, and conclusion receive limited edits, and acknowledgements are added. The main taxonomy and benchmark sections remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–5 retain their content, captions, and visual design. Section 5 replaces run-in labels with standalone numbered headings, producing limited changes in spacing and text layout while preserving the two-column format.

improvement.justification: Section 5.3 makes the previously brief orchestration agenda more concrete and useful by connecting policy selection, memory, verification, training, and evaluation to additional literature. Clearer subsection organization also helps navigation. These gains are concentrated in future directions; the central taxonomy and benchmark synthesis remain unchanged.
